In this figure, triangles ABC and DEF are congruent with BC = EF .

What is the measure of angle EGC ?

Segment BC is the base of triangle ABC, and segment EF is the base of triangle DEF. Vertex A is above the baseline, and vertex D is to the right of A and also above the baseline. options.label: B

The interior angle at vertex A is labeled 70°, and the interior angle at vertex D is labeled 70°.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Two of the triangles below are similar.

[Image: Four triangles labeled I, II, III, IV]

Which two triangles are similar?

options.label: A
options.text: I and II

options.label: B
options.text: I and III

options.label: C
options.text: I and IV

options.label: D
options.text: II and IV

options.label: E
options.text: III and IV

reference_items.figure_description:
Four triangles displayed side by side:
- Triangle I: A scalene obtuse triangle with a horizontal base at the bottom. The top vertex is closer to the left, so the left side is shorter than the right side.
- Triangle II: An acute isosceles triangle with a horizontal top edge. The two longer sides point downward to meet at a sharp vertex at the bottom.
- Triangle III: A tall, thin obtuse triangle with a short horizontal base at the bottom. The left side slants steeply upward to a top vertex, which connects via a long hypotenuse-like side down to the right end of the base.
- Triangle IV: A scalene obtuse triangle with a horizontal top edge, pointing downward to a vertex at the bottom offset to the right. It has the same shape and internal angles as Triangle I, but rotated 180° and reduced in size.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.stem:

The triangles shown are congruent. The measures of some of the sides and angles are given. What is the value of x?
reference_items.figure_description:

The left triangle has a horizontal bottom side. Its left side is labeled "6 cm". The interior angle at the bottom-left vertex is labeled "49°", and the interior angle at the top vertex is labeled "81°".
The right triangle has a nearly horizontal bottom side that slopes slightly downward from right to left, labeled "6 cm". The interior angle at the bottom-right vertex is labeled "81°", and the interior angle at the top vertex is labeled "x°".
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem: Which picture shows that 2/5 is equivalent to 4/10 ?

options.label: A
options.text: [Image: 2-by-5 grid with 4 squares shaded]

options.label: B
options.text: [Image: 2-by-5 grid with 2 squares shaded]

options.label: C
options.text: [Image: 2-by-5 grid with 5 squares shaded in a checkerboard pattern]

options.label: D
options.text: [Image: Rectangle with 2 solid circles and 3 open circles]

reference_items.figure_description:
Four labeled options (A, B, C, D):
- Option A shows a rectangle divided into a 2-by-5 grid of 10 equal squares. The two squares in the first column and the two squares in the fifth column are completely shaded black (4 of 10 squares shaded).
- Option B shows a rectangle divided into a 2-by-5 grid of 10 equal squares. The top-left square (row 1, column 1) and bottom-right square (row 2, column 5) are shaded black (2 of 10 squares shaded).
- Option C shows a rectangle divided into a 2-by-5 grid of 10 equal squares. In the top row, the 1st, 3rd, and 5th squares are shaded black; in the bottom row, the 2nd and 4th squares are shaded black (5 of 10 squares shaded in a checkerboard pattern).
- Option D shows a rectangular box containing five small circles scattered inside: two circles are solid black and three circles are open white circles with a black outline.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: A person looking at a solid made of cubes]

The solid is made of 5 small cubes.
Which shape does the person in the diagram see?

options.label: A
options.text: [Image: A vertical column of three squares with one square attached to the left of the middle square]

options.label: B
options.text: [Image: A vertical column of three squares with one square attached to the right of the middle square]

options.label: C
options.text: [Image: A vertical column of three squares with one square attached to the left of the middle square and one square attached to the right of the top square]

options.label: D
options.text: [Image: A vertical column of three squares with one square attached to the left of the top square and one square attached to the right of the middle square]

reference_items.figure_description:
At the top of the item, a person is standing to the left of a three-dimensional solid made of 5 small identical cubes. The person is shown in side profile facing right toward the solid, with a horizontal dotted line extending from the person's eyes to the top-left cube of the solid. The solid is drawn in isometric projection and consists of:
- A central vertical column of 3 cubes.
- One cube attached to the back-right of the top cube of the column, at the same height as the top cube.
- One cube attached to the front-right of the middle cube of the column, extending forward toward the viewer at the middle height level.

The response options each show a flat 2D shape composed of connected unit squares:
- Option A: 4 squares consisting of a vertical column of 3 squares with 1 square attached to the left of the middle square.
- Option B: 4 squares consisting of a vertical column of 3 squares with 1 square attached to the right of the middle square.
- Option C: 5 squares consisting of a vertical column of 3 squares with 1 square attached to the left of the middle square and 1 square attached to the right of the top square.
- Option D: 5 squares consisting of a vertical column of 3 squares with 1 square attached to the left of the top square and 1 square attached to the right of the middle square.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem: Which shape has a line of symmetry?

options.label: A
options.text: [Image: A trapezoid with two parallel horizontal lines. The right side of the trapezoid is longer than the left hand side.]

options.label: B
options.text: [Image: An isosceles triangle with the base forming a vertical line.]

options.label: C
options.text: [Image: A parallelogram where top and bottom sides are equal in length and the left and right sides are also equal in length.]

options.label: D
options.text: [Image: A right triangle with the 90 degree angle in the bottom left.]

reference_items.figure_description:
Four geometric shapes labeled A through D:
A: A trapezoid with horizontal top and bottom parallel sides; the bottom is longer than the top, and the right slanted side is longer and less steep than the left side.
B: An isosceles triangle with a vertical base on the left and a vertex pointing to the right; the top and bottom sides are marked with equal tick marks.
C: A parallelogram with horizontal top and bottom sides each marked with a single tick mark, and slanted left and right sides each marked with a double tick mark.
D: A scalene right-angled triangle with a vertical left side and a horizontal bottom side, with a right-angle square symbol marked at the lower-left corner.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem: Which shows 2/3 of the square shaded?

options.label: A
options.text: [Image: Square divided horizontally into six equal strips with the top two strips shaded]

options.label: B
options.text: [Image: Square with an unshaded triangle at the bottom and shaded regions above]

options.label: C
options.text: [Image: Square divided vertically into three strips with the two narrow outer strips shaded]

options.label: D
options.text: [Image: Square with an unshaded triangle spanning from the bottom edge to the top center and two shaded triangles on the sides]

options.label: E
options.text: [Image: Square divided vertically into three equal strips with the two outer strips shaded]

reference_items.figure_description:
Five squares, labeled A through E, are shown in a row:
- Square A is divided horizontally into 6 equal strips. The top 2 strips are shaded gray, and the bottom 4 strips are unshaded white.
- Square B has line segments extending from the bottom-left corner to the center, from the bottom-right corner to the center, and from the center to the top-right corner. The triangle formed at the bottom is white, and the remaining area of the square is shaded gray.
- Square C is divided vertically into three regions by two vertical lines: two narrow gray strips on the left and right edges, each approximately one-sixth the width of the square, and a wider unshaded white region in the middle.
- Square D contains an unshaded white isosceles triangle whose base is the bottom edge of the square and whose apex touches the midpoint of the top edge. The two right-triangular regions to the left and right of this triangle are shaded gray.
- Square E is divided vertically into 3 strips of equal width. The leftmost and rightmost strips are shaded gray, and the middle strip is unshaded white.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: Coordinate grid with points M and N]

Two points M and N are shown in the figure above. John is looking for a point P such that MNP is an isosceles triangle. Which of these points could be point P?
reference_items.figure_description: A 6-by-6 grid in the first quadrant of a Cartesian coordinate system. The horizontal x-axis has an arrow pointing to the right, labeled x, with origin O and tick marks labeled 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6. The vertical y-axis has an arrow pointing upwards, labeled y, with tick marks labeled 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6. Grid lines are drawn at each integer value from 1 to 6. Two points are plotted on the grid: point M at (1, 2), labeled M, and point N at (5, 2), labeled N.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics).

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.
